# Chapter 47 — Auditable readings: counts, estimators and covariances {#sec-qjax47-en .unnumbered}

`exact` | `simulated` — Measurement-primitives block. This chapter replaces the idea of an aggregator report with
verifiable pieces: normalization, reading, interval and prior declaration of the estimator. It adds no new API.
Related verifiers: `tools/check_book_api.py`, `tools/check_book_parity.py`.

## 47.1 Why there is no aggregator object (`exact`)

A count does not carry its own contract. What can be registered is the full chain of decisions: which SDK fixed the
bit order, from which probability each quantity is derived, which estimator produces the interval and which phase is
declared in the preparation. Keeping those decisions separate prevents one dict from labelling as "measured" a value
that was actually declared. The primitives already live in the package and are used directly.

## 47.2 Canonicalization and reading (`exact`)

`qang.interop.canonical_counts` returns canonical tuple keys and respects Qiskit and Cirq ordering;
`qang.probability.analyze` turns $k_0$ zeros into a reading with an interval.

```python
from qang.interop import canonical_counts
from qang.probability import analyze
from qang.statistics import qg_estimate

counts = canonical_counts({"0": 750, "1": 250})
reading = analyze(750, 1000)
estimate = qg_estimate(750, 1000, method="wilson")
counts, reading.qg_z, estimate
```

The reading adds no new physics: $qg_Z=2p_0-1$, $\theta=\arccos qg_Z$, $qg_S=H(p_0)$ and $m=2000p_0-1000$.
`qang.probability.readings_from_p0` exposes the same chain when the probability is already known.

## 47.3 Intervals, covariances and witnesses (`exact`)

`qang.statistics.qg_estimate` gathers Bayes, Wilson and delta for $qg_Z$; `qang.statistics.qg_covariance` and
`qang.statistics.register_witness_variance` propagate uncertainty to several qubits;
`qang.statistics.qg_s_estimate`, `qang.statistics.radius2_estimate` and `qang.statistics.direction_estimate` cover
entropy, radius and direction from counts in several bases. Each declares its method: there is no universal interval
that serves every quantity.

## 47.4 Preregistration without an aggregator (`exact`)

Before measuring, one fixes the bit order and qubit 0, the total shot count, the estimator, the confidence level, the
required bases and which phases are declared parameters. A declared phase can be recorded as metadata, but must not
be presented as an estimate from $Z$ counts. The final result is the explicit concatenation of primitives, not a
structure that decides for the user what a "report" means.

## 47.5 Without qang and with qang

| Aspect | Without `qang` | With `qang` (primitives) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Bit order | implicit | `canonical_counts` fixes it per SDK |
| Estimator | rewritten in each analysis | `qg_estimate` declares `bayes`, `wilson` or `delta` |
| Multiqubit variance | hand-made formula | `qg_covariance`, `register_witness_variance` |
| Declared phase | mixed with the reading | recorded separately; $Z$ cannot estimate it |
| Audit | free text | registered chain of functions and parameters |
